object_description: three touching structures with a long classroom wing floating above a pyramid-shaped base
design_condition: three clearly defined structures subtly touch each other and span a covered outdoor space for the all-weather pitch, with the classroom wing lifted 10 to 18 metres above it

positive: Three clearly defined structures accommodate different uses, subtly touch and create a distinctive whole
The structures span a covered outdoor space for the all-weather playground
The complex is memorable and easily followed from the south and west in the dense quarter
Short routes lead from the central entrance hall to the sports and communal uses
High utility value, with multi-purpose hall and canteen combinable
The kindergartens sit at the same level as the indoor recreation room and spacious outdoor areas
The wide 90-metre hall between the classrooms serves as access, checkroom and learning area, zoned by staircase and atrium
The surrounding pergola acts as an escape route and frees the long hall from fire protection requirements
Pergola and tapering roof cleverly make the flying body appear less high than it is
Light-coloured concrete and glass give a coherent appearance
Well thought-out organisation of uses, urban orientation and memorable, spectacular architecture
negative: The kindergarten outdoor areas only see the sun in the evening
The pergola lets users pass in front of the storey-high classroom windows, and its railings raise open questions
The path to the break area is long, without a lift and inaccessible for people with walking difficulties
The in-situ concrete construction high above the pitch can only be built with elaborate temporary structures
The drawn roof and footbridge trusses raise many questions
The load-bearing slabs of the classroom wing represent considerable thermal bridges
The large external development and the many recesses are complex
The deep basement under the pitch must be anchored against buoyancy
The load transfer of the south-facing trusses to the stair towers is unresolved
The effort involved is considerable in both economic and ecological terms
The design leaves many questions unanswered
The generous open space is offered as a fenced pitch rather than a neighbourhood recreation area, so the grand gesture loses its power
